name: GOOGLETRANSLATE
description: GOOGLETRANSLATE translates text from one language to another using Google Translate directly inside a spreadsheet.
tldr: GOOGLETRANSLATE translates text in a cell from a source language to a target language.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The text to translate. Can be a string literal or a cell reference.

parameters.name: source_language
parameters.description: The two-letter language code of the original text, e.g. 'en' for English. If omitted, Google auto-detects the language.

parameters.name: target_language
parameters.description: The two-letter language code to translate into, e.g. 'es' for Spanish. Default is the sheet's locale language.

basicExample.explanation: The text 'Hello' is translated from English ('en') to Spanish ('es').

advancedExamples.title: Translate a whole column
advancedExamples.description: Translate customer feedback from French to English for all rows
advancedExamples.explanation: ARRAYFORMULA applies GOOGLETRANSLATE to each cell in A2:A100.

advancedExamples.title: Auto-detect source language
advancedExamples.description: Translate text without knowing the source language
advancedExamples.explanation: Using 'auto' lets Google detect the source language automatically.

howItWorks: GOOGLETRANSLATE sends the provided text to Google Translate and returns the translated result. It supports two-letter language codes (ISO 639-1). If the source language is omitted, it is auto-detected. If the target language is omitted, the sheet's default language is used.

howToSteps.name: Select the text
howToSteps.text: Click the cell containing the text you want to translate, or type a string literal.

howToSteps.name: Choose languages
howToSteps.text: Provide source and target language codes, e.g. 'en' and 'es'.

howToSteps.name: Copy down if needed
howToSteps.text: Use ARRAYFORMULA or fill down to translate multiple cells.

limitations: GOOGLETRANSLATE is Google Sheets only and has no native Excel equivalent.
It requires an internet connection to call Google Translate.
Translation quality may vary for technical or idiomatic text.
Heavy use may be rate-limited by Google.

commonErrors.cause: Language code is not recognized or is not two letters.
commonErrors.fix: Use valid ISO 639-1 codes such as 'en', 'es', 'fr', 'de', 'zh'.

commonErrors.cause: The text is empty or the source and target languages are the same.
commonErrors.fix: Check that the cell contains text and the languages are different.

commonErrors.cause: The formula is waiting for the Google Translate service to respond.
commonErrors.fix: Wait a moment; if it persists, check your internet connection.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: GOOGLETRANSLATE is exclusive to Google Sheets. Excel has no built-in equivalent; you would need a Microsoft Translator API or Power Query connector.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Language codes are two-letter ISO 639-1 values. 'auto' can be used for source detection.

faq.question: Can I translate an entire sheet?
faq.answer: Yes, wrap GOOGLETRANSLATE in ARRAYFORMULA or copy the formula down a column.

faq.question: Does it work offline?
faq.answer: No, it requires an internet connection to reach Google Translate.

faq.question: What language codes should I use?
faq.answer: Use ISO 639-1 codes like 'en' for English, 'es' for Spanish, 'de' for German, 'fr' for French, 'ja' for Japanese, 'zh' for Chinese.

faq.question: Can I translate in Excel?
faq.answer: Excel has no built-in GOOGLETRANSLATE. You can use the Microsoft Translator add-in or an API call with Power Query.
